children: Brazil's retail sales rose less than expected in August, data from statistics agency IBGE showed on Thursday, as high interest rates continued to weigh on consumer demand in Latin America's largest economy.
Sales grew 0.1% in August from the previous month, with six of the eight sectors tracked by IBGE posting gains
Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 0.7% increase
On an annual basis, retail sales rose 0.4% in the period, also undershooting expectations of a 1.45% gain

Pantheon Macroeconomics' chief Latin America economist Andres Abadia said that the outlook for retail sales remains subdued as high borrowing costs continue to constrain demand, despite recent rate cuts
Central bank policymakers, who in September cut the benchmark interest rate for a fifth straight meeting to 13.75%, will meet again on November 3-4
